title: The role of AI assisted writing feedback in developing secondary students writing skills
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether AI-assisted writing feedback improves the writing performance of secondary-level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students more than traditional teacher feedback alone. The authors focus on a common instructional problem in EFL writing classrooms: teachers often have limited time to provide detailed, individualized feedback, while students need frequent revision opportunities to improve grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and overall writing quality. The study also examines students’ perceptions of using an AI writing assistant as a feedback tool.

The intervention compared two feedback conditions over an 8-week period. The experimental group used Grammarly to receive immediate AI-generated feedback on drafts, including grammar, spelling, punctuation, word choice, style, sentence clarity, and coherence; after revision, the teacher also provided brief higher-order feedback. The control group followed a traditional process in which the teacher provided delayed written feedback on drafts. Both groups completed pre-test and post-test timed persuasive essays and followed the same writing curriculum with the same instructor. Writing was scored analytically across content, organization, language use, and mechanics by two independent EFL raters, and the experimental group also completed a post-study perception questionnaire.

Participants were 60 Turkish public high school students aged 15–17 enrolled in an EFL program, divided into an experimental group and a control group of 30 each. The study took place in a secondary school setting in Türkiye during regular class time, with use of the school computer lab for the AI tool. Students had little prior experience with AI-based writing tools, and parental consent was obtained because participants were minors.

The main conclusion is that AI-assisted feedback significantly improved students’ writing more than teacher-only feedback. The experimental group showed larger gains in total writing scores, especially in language use and organization, while both groups improved over time. Students also reported positive perceptions of the AI tool, including improved confidence and satisfaction with the feedback. The authors conclude that AI writing tools can effectively supplement secondary EFL writing instruction, particularly when combined with teacher guidance rather than used as a replacement for human feedback.
